page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server featuring one NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 24 GB of VRAM. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this configuration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference, achieving 11,784.81 tokens per second for prompt processing on small 135M models and 2,225.82 tokens per second on medium 7B models. Conversely, standard CPU benchmarks such as Geekbench and single-core stress-ng tests fall into the bottom 25% tier. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations on Redis consistently register in the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 offers a specialized resource profile that trades raw CPU processing power for high-density GPU acceleration. This makes it highly efficient for workloads that can offload computation to the NVIDIA L4 GPU, such as machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM execution, and GPU-driven graphics tasks. It is less optimal for CPU-heavy compilation, text processing, or storage-intensive databases due to the lack of local storage and lower CPU single-core performance.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It features a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM alongside an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of system memory. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark data shows that while the server exhibits lower-tier single-core and multi-core CPU performance, it delivers top-tier results in large language model inference, processing 2,225.82 tokens per second for medium 7B models. This hardware profile provides a cost-efficient balance for organizations requiring dedicated GPU acceleration without the overhead of massive CPU configurations. It is best suited for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, and graphics processing, rather than CPU-bound or storage-heavy applications.
